**Step 1 — Scene:** A mixed plate of pizza pieces, skin-on fish, lentils and a few leafy greens.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A large square dinner plate, approximately 27 cm across. Allowing for its rounded corners and perspective, I’ll use a circular-equivalent diameter of about 28 cm: area ≈ **615 cm²**. Food on the neighboring plates is excluded.

**Step 3 — Items:** Tomato-and-onion pizza, cheese pizza, cooked skin-on fish, cooked lentils with vegetable bits, leafy greens, and a light visible oil coating. Pizza toppings are included in the pizza estimates.

**Steps 4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy:**

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = volume | Density → weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Tomato-and-onion pizza, two pieces | 18% | 111 cm² × 1.1 cm = 122 ml | 0.9 → 110 g | 240 | 264 kcal |
| Cheese pizza, overlapping pieces | 23% | 141 cm² × 1.0 cm = 141 ml | 0.9 → 127 g | 275 | 349 kcal |
| Skin-on fish | 23% | 141 cm² × 1.3 cm = 184 ml | 1.0 → 184 g | 190 | 350 kcal |
| Lentils and vegetable bits | 12% | 74 cm² × 1.4 cm = 103 ml | 0.8 → 83 g | 115 | 95 kcal |
| Leafy greens | 3% | 18 cm² × 1.5 cm = 28 ml | 0.15 → 4 g | 20 | 1 kcal |
| Light oil coating | Overlays food | Approximately 4 ml | 1.0 → 4 g | 884 | 35 kcal |

The food footprints total **79%** of the plate; the oil overlays these areas rather than occupying additional plate area.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **512 g and 1,094 kcal** is plausible for several pizza pieces plus a substantial fish-and-lentil portion. The few leaves contribute very little weight. Fish type, pizza thickness and oil quantity are the main uncertainties.
